what: Route 1, run 2 (+180): the same 7000 ms step length that passed cleanly at +120 FAILS criterion 2a badly at +180 (5.64 deg/s apart on the last two step rates, vs 0.11 at +120). The step-rate sequence oscillates rather than climbing-then-flattening. 2b still passes. This means convergence at 7000 ms is angular-speed-dependent, not a fixed constant that generalizes across commands.
predeclaration: docs/phase2-route1-step-extension-predeclared-20260830.md section 7 (a pass at +120 authorizes exactly this repeat at +180, same step length)
verdict: FAIL. Criterion 2a fails badly. tau_actuator_s=2.162s must NOT be quoted as settled -- the step phase never reached a stable rate.

run.label: baseline 3000 / step 7000 / settle 5000, +180, max_travel_m=4.5 -- identical phases to the passing +120 run, only step_angular_speed changed
run.reason_field_confirmed_correct: Second real-hardware confirmation of the fix in commit af5f547f, agreeing with the raw evidence (aborted_early=False, 0/148 tripped, full 15001.6 ms of 15000 ms window) with no manual correction needed.

analysis_raw.interpretation: tau_actuator_s = |rotation after commanding angular 0| / steady rate during the step. Compare it against the ~1 s decision period: well below means the dead time is dominated by the OBSERVER and damping cannot fix it; comparable or above means real actuator carryover.
analysis_raw.caveats: n is small by construction at ~1 Hz. Do NOT fit a turn-rate law to this, and do NOT reuse omega as a calibration constant -- the 2026-08-26 guarded-turn measurement showed a 2.6x spread on identical stationary parameters.

run.analysis_caveat: tau_actuator_s=2.162s and omega_step_deg_per_s=-10.6527 do not meet criterion 2a and must not be quoted as a clean measurement.

1_report_stream_ready.evidence: started/continuous_started true, ready true, no readiness_reason.

2_step_reaches_steady_rotation_2a.requirement: >=3 informative intervals AND last two step rates agree within 1.5 deg/s
2_step_reaches_steady_rotation_2a.note: No climb-then-flatten shape like the +120 pass. The sequence oscillates across the whole step phase (roughly -8 to -15 deg/s with no convergent trend), the largest single-run failure margin of any run today.

3_settle_goes_flat_2b.requirement: >=3 informative intervals AND last two settle rates agree within 1.5 deg/s
3_settle_goes_flat_2b.note: Settle converges cleanly again, as in both prior settle-passing runs, despite the step phase never settling. The settle mechanism appears robust regardless of the step's own convergence.

4_containment_and_stop.evidence: 0 of 148 samples outside the 10.0 m corridor. stop_result.ok=true, ack.movement_ok=true.

5_travel_guard_does_not_trip.evidence: 0 of 148 samples carry travel_guard_tripped:true; motion_refresh.aborted_early=False; cumulative_travel_m 2.9536 of the 4.5 m budget. reason field correctly read 'window_complete' -- second real-hardware confirmation of the fix.

6_gate_disarmed_after_verified.evidence: enabled:false, real_motion_allowed:false, no active session, verified from both the live API and RAW core.config_entries after the documented ~15s propagation delay.

what_this_establishes.convergence_is_angular_speed_dependent: The 7000 ms step length that let the +120 run converge cleanly (0.11 deg/s residual) does NOT generalize to +180 (5.64 deg/s residual, no convergent trend visible). Whatever combination of onset lag, mechanical response, and telemetry noise the +120 pass overcame, it did not simply scale with the +50% larger commanded angular speed.
what_this_establishes.magnitude_scales_roughly_as_expected: omega_step_deg_per_s went -6.12 (+120) -> -10.65 (+180), a larger magnitude at the larger command, qualitatively consistent with prior findings that rotation rate increases with commanded angular speed in this band -- but this is a directional observation, not a fitted law, and the underlying step-rate sequence at +180 is too noisy to trust for any quantitative scaling claim.
what_this_establishes.settle_is_robust: This is the third run today where the settle phase converged cleanly (0.26, 1.44, and now 0.77 deg/s residuals) regardless of what happened in the step phase before it -- settle at 5000 ms looks solid across all three attempts.

caveats.n_equals_1: Single run at +180 with this step length. The oscillating step-rate sequence could in principle be one noisy run rather than a repeatable property of +180 -- but note it looks qualitatively different from chord noise (a real, large-amplitude oscillation, not small perturbations around a trend), unlike anything the +120 pass showed.
caveats.what_is_NOT_authorized: Per the step-extension predeclaration, a pass at +120 authorized exactly this one repeat at +180. Neither a pass nor a fail here authorizes anything further -- not a second step_ms increase for +180 specifically, not Phase 2 steering, not the feed-forward design document.

safety.corridor: 10.0 m square, re-scanned and re-verified at the mower's live position (6.0038, -5.3077) after a supervised repositioning drive -- see repositioning_drive below.
safety.operator_confirmation: explicit go/no-go confirmation taken immediately before dispatch (on-site, supervising, area clear, blades off)

repositioning_drive.why: The mower (moved by the operator between runs) sat at (3.8728, -7.4005), where the worst-case clearance was only 3.841 m against the 5.0 m required disk (0.77x) -- insufficient for a fresh 10.0 m corridor.
repositioning_drive.method: raw_pymammotion_execute_vector_segment, the accepted closed-loop reach profile (docs/accepted-profile.json), verified key-by-key identical before real dispatch.
repositioning_drive.outcome: Single call, 4 turn commands and 12 linear commands, target_reached at 0.073 m from (5.98, -5.24) -- the tightest landing of any repositioning drive today.
